content.content: When the deccy CLI persists a draft's durable state, the deccy CLI shall write it to one work-state registry under `.deccy/work/`, untracked with the rest of the `.deccy/` state directory.
content.rationale: Both clauses land on an answer a prerequisite has already settled, so the requirement fixes which side of each answer the write must take rather than reopening the choice. The trigger is the write of durable draft state, not a named verb: which command writes it is not this decision's to pick, and ulqqklzk leaves draft commands to the decisions that own them. The destination clause says one registry under `.deccy/work/` because ulqqklzk already places draft state in a single registry there; a per-draft directory, a path elsewhere under the state directory or a file outside it would each be a competing answer to that settled question, so the requirement names the one place instead of enumerating exclusions. The tracking clause says untracked with the rest of the `.deccy/` state directory because xxwtnpzz makes the state directory untracked as a whole: a registry written into it cannot be tracked without departing from that, and putting the boundary under the directory rather than under the registry keeps this requirement from re-deciding the mechanism that holds it. Keying, entry lifetime, entry contents and read or landing behaviour are left unstated — ulqqklzk defers them, and naming them here would make this requirement the owner of choices that have to change without it.
